# Escape does not cancel a drag once it has crossed into another window

## Context

**Operator's hand run, 2026-09-26** (with #19278): dragging a tab inside the main window and pressing Esc recovers the previous state. It does not when the popup proxy (a converted vessel) is active, or when the tab proxy stands inside a different window.

## The Problem

The cancel itself already works across windows. `DragCoordinator#onDragCancel` leaves the remote target, resets the vessel conversion (`sourceSortZone.resetVesselConversion`) and clears the native-window drop candidates.

What fails is delivery. Escape is heard only by the main-thread `DragDrop` addon of the window where the gesture started:
- `onKeyDown` fires only when `event.key === 'Escape' && me.dragZoneId`.
- `dragZoneId` is set in that window's own `onDragStart`.

During a converted or cross-window drag, the keyboard focus is in another window, the vessel or the target popup. Its `DragDrop` has no `dragZoneId`, so Escape is dropped.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs`: `onKeyDown` (a global capture listener, `addGlobalEventListeners`) holds the Escape guard. It sets `dragCancelled`, cancels a resize, and sends one `drag:cancel` carrying the zone id. Its remote API (`remote.app`) has no cancel entry.
- `src/manager/DomEvent.mjs`: routes a `drag:cancel` to `Neo.get(data.dragZoneId).onDragCancel`, and ignores one without a zone. `fire()` receives the worker message; its `windowId` rides on the message (`worker.Manager#sendMessage`), not in `data`.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs`: `activeSourceZone` is set only when `onDragMove` enters an admitted target, and cleared on void (`handleVoid`). While a conversion is pending, the coordinator cannot name the gesture's owner (@neo-gpt's source read, confirmed).
- The one authority valid in every phase is the window whose `DragDrop` holds `dragZoneId`.

## The Fix

1. `DragDrop` gains a remote `cancelDrag()`. It runs the Escape guard's cancel branch for the gesture this window owns, and it is a no-op without one or when the gesture is already cancelled.
2. Escape in a window without a gesture of its own sends one `drag:cancel` marked `crossWindow` and carrying no zone id. The key's default stays with that window's UI.
3. `DomEvent` hands such a message, with the message's `windowId`, to `DragCoordinator#cancelCrossWindowGesture`. It asks every other app window to `cancelDrag`. It reads no gesture state, so a pending conversion cannot hide the owner.

From there the existing path runs unchanged: the owner's `drag:cancel`, `TabSortZone#onDragCancel` (which retires a converted or still-transitioning vessel), then `DragCoordinator#onDragCancel`.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Neo.main.addon.DragDrop#cancelDrag` (new, `remote.app`) | this ticket | Cancels the gesture this window owns: `dragCancelled` set, a resize cancelled, one `drag:cancel` with `dragZoneId` | No gesture, or already cancelled: sends nothing | JSDoc | AC-3 |
| `drag:cancel` marked `crossWindow` (new payload) | this ticket | Sent by `DragDrop#onKeyDown` on Escape when this window owns no gesture; no `preventDefault` | Sent on every such Escape, drag or not: one message, plus one no-op `cancelDrag` per other window of a multi-window app; none in a single-window app | JSDoc | AC-1, AC-2 |
| `DragCoordinator#cancelCrossWindowGesture` (new) | this ticket | Asks `cancelDrag` of every `Neo.apps` window except the one that heard Escape | A rejected remote call (e.g. a closing window) is swallowed | JSDoc | AC-2 |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 (unit, red first): `DragDrop#onKeyDown` without a local gesture sends one `drag:cancel` marked `crossWindow`, without `preventDefault`. The local-gesture path is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-2 (unit, red first): a `crossWindow` cancel in the shape `worker.Manager#sendMessage` posts (the `windowId` on the message) asks `cancelDrag` of every other app window, and not of the window that heard Escape.
- [ ] AC-3 (unit): `DragDrop#cancelDrag` cancels the owned gesture once, with one `drag:cancel` carrying the zone id. A second call, or a call without a gesture, sends nothing.
- [ ] AC-4 (runtime): pressing Escape on the target window's page during a converted drag restores the pre-drag layout: the tab back at its source and no vessel left. It is measured headless, with #19288's screen flag, in the large-over-small journey.
- [ ] AC-5 (unit, pin): a cancel while the conversion is still pending (`transitioning`, no target admitted) retires the vessel as a converted cancel does. The behaviour already exists; the arm pins it, and dropping `transitioning` from `TabSortZone#onDragCancel` fails it.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The operator's hand run: Esc during a vessel or cross-window tab proxy drag recovers the previous state.
